clue.text: Simple artist's note in front of a catalogue

indicators.note: the note comes in front of the rest, so it is placed first in the charade

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note
a list is a catalogue of items

explanation.surface: An artist's plain note sits at the front of an exhibition catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Simple artist' is the definition, followed by the link 's; 'note' looks like a written message but is the musical minim.
explanation.definitionFit: A minimalist is an artist working with pared-down, spare forms.

clue.text: From what we hear, compelled to be a domestic

indicators.note: the phrase signals that a word is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: compelled means made, as in made to do something

explanation.surface: Gossip says someone was forced into domestic service.
explanation.definitionFit: A maid is a household servant, which is what a domestic means as a noun.

clue.text: One has no reason to take action in support of staff's union

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so it comes second

parts.note: NUT is the National Union of Teachers, a British union for school staff
a case is a legal action brought in court

explanation.surface: Someone is told there is no reason for industrial action backing the staff union.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'in support of' puts CASE underneath NUT. NUT, the National Union of Teachers, was a well-known British teaching union.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutcase is slang for a lunatic, someone who has lost their reason.

clue.text: Bold use may be made of this sporting event

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the word for pairs shaken up, which is what the answer describes

explanation.surface: Daring tactics might be used in this tennis event.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: the answer, read as wordplay, tells you to jumble DOUBLES, and that jumble gives BOLD USE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mixed doubles is a tennis or badminton event with a man and woman on each side.

clue.text: On other side in the French game

indicators.note: the first phrase is placed in the middle of the French article

parts.note: le is French for the
across means on the other side, as across the road

explanation.surface: A French game played on the far side of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a field sport played with netted sticks.

clue.text: Get fed up about half measure in governing body

indicators.note: the satisfying word goes around the half measure, enclosing it

parts.note: to sate is to feed fully or satiate
an en is a printer's measure half the width of an em

explanation.surface: Someone becomes fed up over a half-hearted policy in government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get fed up' sounds like annoyance but means filled up, satiated; an en is half an em in printing.
explanation.definitionFit: A senate is a legislative assembly that governs a state.

clue.text: Voiced support for examination

definitions.meaning: a ... is an oral examination, short for ... voce

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an Italian cheer and the oral exam held at universities.

clue.text: In demand? That's not true

parts.note: to exact is to demand payment or effort

explanation.surface: Is something popular? That is false.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In demand' looks like the phrase meaning popular, but it splits into IN and a verb meaning demand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inexact is imprecise, so not strictly accurate.

clue.text: Not crazy about silver? It's very fashionable

indicators.note: the sane phrase goes around the silver symbol, holding it inside

parts.note: all there means mentally sound
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone is not wild about silver jewellery, yet it is the current fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not crazy about' looks like mild dislike, but it is a phrase for sane wrapped about the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: All the rage is an idiom for whatever is currently in vogue.

clue.text: Deeply involved with team, is unable to drink

parts.note: into means keen on or absorbed in
XI is eleven, a cricket or football team
can't means is unable

explanation.surface: Someone wrapped up in their team can't touch alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: An intoxicant is an alcoholic beverage or anything that makes one drunk.

clue.text: Fit for Centre Court? Just the opposite

definitions.meaning: the central space in a law court in front of the judge

explanation.surface: Is a player fit for Wimbledon's main court? Quite the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Centre Court is Wimbledon's tennis show court, but here it means the middle of a law court; 'Just the opposite' says the clue reads 'Centre Court for fit'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means healthy and also names the open area in the centre of a courtroom.

clue.text: Group set up to investigate Labour

definitions.meaning: a committee formed to study a question
Labour is the British party of the workers, punningly a party that works

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a study committee, and jokingly the Labour Party, a party of working people.

clue.text: Declared second-hand

parts.note: a hand is help, as in lend a hand

explanation.surface: Goods described as used.
explanation.definitionFit: Said is the past tense of say, meaning stated or announced.

clue.text: Coming back from fight, a poet sought healer

indicators.note: Coming back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A poet seeks a healer after a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The run HTAPOETSO sits inside 'fight, a poet sought'; 'Coming back' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An osteopath is a practitioner who treats ailments by manipulating bones and muscles.

clue.text: Page about joints going into detail

parts.note: articular means relating to the joints

explanation.surface: A page on the body's joints goes into specifics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a container signal, but 'about joints' together means articular.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular is a single item or point, so a detail.

clue.text: It's hard, with a lion around, to avail oneself of this watering-hole

indicators.note: the lion goes around the hard letter, enclosing it

parts.note: Leo is the lion of the zodiac
h is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
to use something is to avail oneself of it

explanation.surface: With a lion nearby, it is tough to make use of this drinking spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watering-hole' suggests where a lion drinks, but it is slang for a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: An alehouse is a tavern, and watering-hole is jocular slang for a pub.

clue.text: Sportsman fishes river

parts.note: skate are flat fishes, and the plural is the same

explanation.surface: An angler fishes a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fishes' reads as a verb but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A skater is someone who competes on ice or wheels, an athlete.

clue.text: Sang with evil manipulation, as 18 did with this man's

indicators.note: manipulation says the letters of the two words are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A singer performed under sinister control, as Trilby did under this man's.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is TRILBY, heroine of George du Maurier's novel, who sang under the hypnotic control of this man.
explanation.definitionFit: In the novel, the hypnotist turns the heroine into a singer by mesmerism, so she sang with evil manipulation of his.

clue.text: Attempt to collect one pound in a hat

indicators.note: the attempt word gathers the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a try is an attempt
I is the Roman numeral for one
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: Someone tries to collect a pound coin in a hat, like a busker.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilby is a soft felt hat with an indented crown.

clue.text: Christian's statement of his rank, in Muslim country

definitions.meaning: Fletcher Christian of the Bounty was a master's mate
a state ruled by an imam

explanation.walkthrough: Christian is Fletcher Christian, mutineer on HMS Bounty, whose rank was master's mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Split into words it is a mate's self-description; whole, it is territory governed by an Islamic leader.

clue.text: Boy in uniform, note, for service

parts.note: even means uniform or regular
a son is a boy
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: A boy in uniform carries a note to church.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the evening church service of the Anglican Church.

clue.text: A canoe I built for this island group

indicators.note: built says the letters are constructed into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone built a canoe to voyage around Pacific islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceania is the collective name for the Pacific islands, a region.

clue.text: Overturning a republic, became monarch

indicators.note: overturning in a down clue means the combined letters are read from the bottom upward

parts.note: Niger is a West African republic

explanation.surface: After overthrowing a republic, someone made themselves king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overturning' sounds like a coup but turns A NIGER upside down to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Regina is Latin for queen, a reigning female sovereign.

clue.text: Lizard difficult to see from helm — ocean is rough

indicators.note: rough suggests disturbed water, telling us the letters are churned

explanation.surface: From the helm, a sailor can't see a lizard as the sea is rough.
explanation.definitionFit: The chameleon is a lizard that changes colour to blend into its surroundings.

clue.text: This piper should have been, as cockney might say

indicators.note: a London cockney accent pronounces the vowel of the paying word like this

parts.note: the ... Piper of Hamelin was never given his fee, so he should have been paid

explanation.surface: This piper deserved something, as a Londoner would put it.
explanation.walkthrough: In the legend the town of Hamelin refused to pay the Pied Piper; a cockney says paid as something like pied.
explanation.definitionFit: Pied, meaning multicoloured, is the epithet of the piper of Hamelin in the folk tale.

clue.text: River or brook

definitions.meaning: a river in north-east England, flowing through Durham

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a Durham river and is informal British for putting up with something.

clue.text: Composer's not hardhearted — his compositions are amusing

indicators.note: the middle letter standing for hard is removed from the heart of the composer's name

parts.note: Franz Lehar was the Hungarian composer of The Merry Widow

explanation.surface: A composer is kind-hearted, and his works are funny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not hardhearted' looks like a character note but drops H, hard, from the middle of LEHAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear wrote nonsense verse and limericks, comic works.

clue.text: Again orders change, nonetheless, to do this?

definitions.text: Again orders change, nonetheless, to do this?

parts.words: Again orders change, nonetheless, to do this?
parts.note: to rearrange is to put in order again; the same word with its re- swapped for a negative prefix means to upset order

explanation.surface: Orders are changed yet again, so why bother?
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging orders things again; the answer is what you do when order changes for the worse.
explanation.definitionFit: To disarrange is to throw into disorder, the opposite of putting things in order.

clue.text: Regretted beginning from Dieppe, on the way from France

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: rue is French for street

indicators.note: beginning from picks the opening letter of the port's name

explanation.surface: Someone regrets setting off from Dieppe on the road from France.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue is to feel sorrow over, so rued is regretted in the past tense.

clue.text: Pride without prejudice in this novel

parts.note: vanity is excessive pride
fair means unbiased

explanation.surface: Pride appears without Prejudice in this book, unlike Austen's title.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods at Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice; the answer is Thackeray's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanity Fair is a novel by William Makepeace Thackeray.
